item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J00650","case1_error":"Uses the first day's total flowers, 50, as its tulip count, counting the 20 roses again as tulips.","case2_error":"Relabels all four dogs' daily food total as one dog's consumption, then multiplies by four again.","reason":"Both treat an aggregate as a component amount and consequently count quantities already included in that aggregate again.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J00651","case1_error":"Adds the two parent lambs again even though they are included in the original six.","case2_error":"Models the reported count with an invalid equation doubling the entire real population instead of adding eight duplicates and subtracting three omissions.","reason":"The first duplicates an already included subgroup; the second constructs an incorrect equation relating actual and observed counts.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00652","case1_error":"Calculates the cost of one company's ten ads and reports it as the combined cost for three companies.","case2_error":"Correctly calculates Billy's $8 contribution, then unjustifiably halves it to $4.","reason":"The first omits aggregation across three companies; the second adds an unwarranted equal split after calculating the requested individual contribution.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00653","case1_error":"Counts only two houses when the requested total includes Zion and his two friends.","case2_error":"Reports the number of 150-can batches as minutes, omitting the eight minutes required per batch.","reason":"The first omits a participant from the total; the second confuses a batch count with elapsed time by dropping the time conversion.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00654","case1_error":"Gives correct group-product formulas, then introduces unsupported numbers and an unjustified four-term sum yielding 112.","case2_error":"No clear error: $140 correctly totals four weekly deposits starting at $20; the precise month endpoint is ambiguous.","reason":"The first has unsupported numerical work. The second reasonably answers cumulative savings; the reference instead reports a later weekly deposit amount.","judgment":"uncertain"}]}
